newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese completes first solo trek across Arctic.
newsitem.headline: Japanese completes first solo trek across Arctic.

text.p: Japanese adventurer Mitsuro Oba completed the world's first solo crossing of the frozen Arctic Sea, the daily Asahi Shimbun reported on Tuesday.
Oba's expedition headquarters said Oba arrived at Canada's Ward Hunt Island late on Monday, 121 days after he left Russia's Komsomolets Island on the other side of the Arctic Sea, the Asahi reported.
Oba, 44, contacted friends by radio from his base camp in Canada to tell them that he had arrived at the island, the office told the Asahi.
It was the adventurer's fourth attempt since 1994 to cross the Arctic on foot and on skis. Oba lost all of his toes to frostbite in a failed attempt in 1995, the Asahi said.
A British expedition on dog sleds was the first team to cross the frozen Arctic Sea in 1969.
Another British-led international team was the first to cross the Arctic circle on foot and on skis in 1989, but Oba was the first to complete a solo trip.

Oba used a satellite location confirmation system to let his office know his whereabouts during his 1,850-km (1,150-mile) trek. He left Russia's Komsomolets Island on February 23 and walked over the North Pole on May 3.
Oba received supplies via air drop four times, the newspaper said.
